subject: URGENT: Protect SLC Residents and Oppose ICE Expansion
comment: To Mayor Erin Mendenhall and the Salt Lake City Council, I am writing to you today as a concerned resident of Salt Lake City to express my deep alarm regarding the escalating federal immigration enforcement actions across the country and their direct impact on our local community. The recent news of a proposed 7,500-bed ICE detention facility in a West-side warehouse is unconscionable. Furthermore, the tragic killing of Renee Good by immigration officers in Minnesota serves as a harrowing reminder of the dangers posed by aggressive, unchecked federal enforcement. We cannot allow our city to become a hub for such operations or a place where our neighbors live in constant fear. While I appreciate the public concerns already raised by Mayor Mendenhall regarding infrastructure and the vocal opposition from members of the Council, I am imploring you to use every ounce of your executive and legislative authority to go further: * Enforce Land-Use and Zoning Barriers: I urge you to utilize the city's land-use authority and regulatory review processes to block the conversion of any local property into a federal detention or processing center. * Codify "Sensitive Climate" Protections: Please support and advocate for measures like SB136 (the "ICE Out" bill) to ensure that city-owned spaces, libraries, and health centers remain safe zones where federal agents are restricted from enforcement. * Strengthen Non-Cooperation Policies: Ensure that the Salt Lake City Police Department maintains a strict wall between local law enforcement and federal immigration actions, particularly regarding the use of city resources or the honoring of civil detainers without a judicial warrant. * Public Advocacy: Use your platform to formally call upon the federal government and our state's congressional delegation to halt the expansion of detention facilities and investigate the conduct of agents involved in recent violent incidents. Salt Lake City has a proud history of being a welcoming place for those seeking a better life. I'm a transplant from the Akron, OH area and have loved living in this city and exploring what the state has to offer. We are now raising daughters who will soon be of school-age. Community safety is paramount for all - especially for our children and those who don't have the means or access to protect themselves. We must ensure that "stability, compassion, and respect" are not just words, but the lived reality for every resident, regardless of their status. Standing up to a tyrannical government with essentially unlimited funds isn't easy, but it is the right thing to do as our elected leaders. Let your conscience guide you. I look forward to seeing the Council take formal action on these matters in your upcoming sessions. Sincerely, Eric Figliomeni / District 6 /

subject: Opposition to name change of Harvey Milk Blvd.
comment: I am a Salt Lake County resident with strong ties to Salt Lake City and writing to express my strong opposition and outrage to the proposal to rename Harvey Milk Boulevard. If the intent were truly to honor another individual, there are numerous unnamed streets or new developments where that could be done. Choosing instead to replace an existing honorary designation is not neutral. It is a symbolic act, and symbols matter. This proposal does not add to our shared history—it attempts to overwrite it. Harvey Milk Boulevard represents more than a name. It stands for visibility, dignity, and the hard-won recognition of LGBTQ+ people who were historically and currently still are excluded, silenced, or erased. To single out this street for replacement sends a clear message that such recognition is provisional and can be revoked for political reasons. Equally concerning is the precedent this sets. Street naming has long been a matter of local governance. State-level intervention in this process undermines local control and disregards the voices of the residents who live, work, and conduct business in this community. This issue is not about partisan preference. It is about whether we choose coexistence over erasure, and whether our government uses its authority to unify or to provoke. Salt Lake City is capable of honoring multiple histories without diminishing any of them. I hope you will consider not just the policy implications of this proposal but the message it sends to those who rely on public symbols to know they belong. Thank you for your time and consideration. Sincerely, Karen Stagnaro Salt Lake County resident

subject: Concerns of ICE facility construction in Utah
comment: To Whom It May Concern, I write to urge the council to consider and pass an emergency ordinance requiring a conditional use permit for ICE facilities in SLC, giving the council and planning commission the legal basis to block the construction and use of detention facilities in SLC. As you may know, ICE detention facilities are inhumane, neglecting to feed, medicate, or otherwise care for those they detain. (https://www.cbsnews.com/atlanta/news/ice-stopped-paying-for-detainee-medical-care-as-population-surged/). As ICE has now begun to detain and hold children in these facilities as well, these detention centers become a massive human rights violation via the abuse and neglect of both children and adults. Additionally, these facilities allow U.S. citizens (including children) to be flown out of state, away from home or legal assistance. (https://www.cnn.com/2026/01/24/us/elvis-tipan-echeverria-toddler-ice-arrest-minnesota) The SLC City Council is responsible for protecting its constituents from such human rights abuses and danger. Thank you, Selja Engar District # 34 and 14.
